summary: Regional egress flap caused routing fallback to remote region resulting in streaming hangs and elevated p95 latencies
description:
Issue summary:
A subset of NexaChat production traffic originating in us-west started experiencing increased p50/p95 latencies and frequent streaming WebSocket stalls around 2026-03-10 02:10 UTC. Customers reported generation streams freezing for 5-30s and occasional final response timeouts.

Impact:
- NexaChat customers (10+ apps) observed degraded streaming UX and token timeouts.
- Elevated token cost due to retrying behaviors.
- Triage flagged as P1 / Sev1 because dedicated capacity customer had SLA expectations.

Environment:
- Redwood prod (hosted) serving cluster: rw-infer-us-west-a (primary), rw-infer-eu-west-b (fallback)
- Affected regions: us-west (primary), failover to eu-west for some requests
- Affected models: rw-bert-13b, rw-chat-3b (customer pinned to latest stable)

Steps to reproduce / Observed behavior:
1) Start a streaming chat session from a NexaChat instance in us-west region.
2) Observe initial tokens stream correctly then stall after ~8-12s on ~1 in 6 requests.
3) Server-side logs show long tail on final chunk and occasional 504/502 from edge proxy.

Logs / metrics snippets (sanitized):
- edge-proxy[us-west] 2026-03-10T02:12:14Z: upstream_error=502, conn_id=42a1f
- serving-runtime: token_delay_ms p95 rose from 120ms -> 1.8s between 02:08-02:18 UTC
- nat-gateway-us-west-4: CPU 95pct, conntrack near max (7.9M/8M) around 02:09 UTC
- control-plane routing: observed traffic shift 14% -> eu-west for customer prefix at 02:10 UTC

Preliminary investigation notes:
- Correlation between NAT gateway saturation (conntrack exhaustion) and a subset of requests being routed to eu-west fallback cluster. The fallback increased RTT and exposed streaming timeouts.
- BGP/peering telemetry from provider shows a short withdrawal from primary egress peer for a /24 used by our us-west egress IPs at 02:08-02:11 UTC. Upstream provider logs show flapping.
- Edge proxy retries sometimes re-open connections to eu-west resulting in higher latency and TLS renegotiation overhead; streaming backpressure leads to client perceived stalls.

Workaround applied:
- Temporarily applied a per-customer routing override to pin NexaChat traffic to remaining healthy us-west egress IPs while we scale NAT and work with provider. This reduced stalls for the customer.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: Increase conntrack table size and provision additional NAT capacity in us-west (in-progress).
- Network: Open escalation with upstream transit provider for BGP flap root cause and request monitored mitigation.
- Runtime: Add health gating on fallback routing so streaming sessions are less likely to be migrated mid-session.
- CS: Notify NexaChat of mitigation and provide timeline for permanent fix.

Related incident: INC-20260310-71

2026-03-11 09:12 UTC - Network Eng (L. Rivera): Opened ticket with transit provider (TP-9872) for BGP instability; provider acknowledged and is investigating flapping during 02:08-02:12 UTC window.
2026-03-12 14:40 UTC - Runtime Eng (S. O'Neil): Implemented conservative gating on fallback routing in staging to avoid mid-session region migration; PR under review (#3214).

resolution_notes: Mitigation reduced impact: NAT capacity increased and per-customer routing pin prevented fallback. Waiting on upstream provider root-cause confirmation and runtime fallback gating rollout to close.
